subject: Dedicated shoulder pool resilience plan and transient burst proposal for VelaAI
messages:
From: Nina Park <nina@velaai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Cicely Ramos <cicely@velaai.com>, Amit Suresh <amit.s@velaai.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 launch demand — shoulder pool / transient burst ask

Hi Priyom,

We're ramping up for a major feature launch in November and our traffic projections show brief but steep peaks (10x) during the first 72 hours post-launch. Attached is a conservative demand projection for Q4. Two asks:

1) Can Redwood provide a short-term burst policy for our Dedicated tenancy that guarantees additional GPU capacity for short windows without requiring a long-term reserve? We're looking for a predictable fallback for 2–6 hour spikes.

2) What operational guardrails do you recommend for autoscale to avoid noisy-neighbor evictions while keeping tail latency under 350ms for our chat endpoints?

We don't expect continuous sustained usage at the higher rate, but we need reliability during the spike. Budget-wise, procurement wants a ballpark delta for transient usage (per-hour rate) vs adding reserved units.

Can we hop on a quick call Monday to align?

Thanks,
Nina Park
Head of Platform — VelaAI
[Attachment: VelaAI_Demand_Projection_Q4_2027.xlsx]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina@velaai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 launch demand — shoulder pool / transient burst ask

Nina — thank you for the projection, that helps a lot. High-level response below; happy to unpack on a call.

Summary of options (short):
- Shoulder pool (soft commit): carve a small reserved slab for baseline, plus a "shoulder" allocation we can prioritize for VelaAI from a shared transient pool. Fast to enable, predictable throttles.
- Transient burst credits: per-hour usage priced at a premium; no long-term commit but subject to availability and preemption rules.
- Hybrid addendum: small reserved commit for steady-state + X hours/month of guaranteed burst with pre-warming and priority scheduling.

Operational guardrails we recommend:
- Headroom multiplier: target 25–35% autoscale headroom for chat workloads; increase to 40% for launch windows.
- Eviction policy: prefer graceful preemption with 60s drain and KV cache checkpointing; avoid hard kills for live sessions.
- Pre-warming: schedule warm-up calls 15–30 minutes before expected spike windows to populate KV caches and reduce cold-starts.

I've attached our draft terms for transient bursts (redwood-burst-terms-v1.pdf) — pricing examples and typical SLA language are in section 2.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Monday 10/11 at 11:00 PT. If that works, I'll include Karthik and Marissa to nail the sizing and ops steps.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-burst-terms-v1.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Nina Park <nina@velaai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 launch demand — shoulder pool / transient burst ask

On Sun, Oct 10, 2027 at 12:03 PM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
> Summary of options (short):

Adding some detail from infra/serving perspective so expectations are clear:
- Baseline sizing: based on the spreadsheet, recommend a minimum reserved slab equivalent to 4 GPU units (serving-optimized A100-equivalent capacity) to stabilize steady-state.
- Burst headroom: provide access to an extra 6 GPU units from the shared transient pool with priority queuing for up to 4 hours/day during the launch window. That should cover ~95% of projected peaks.
- Preemption behavior: transient pool may be preempted when overall global demand exceeds capacity — we'll set a VelaAI priority token to minimize preemption likelihood during your agreed windows.
- Autoscale tuning:
  * Target latency: keep p99 under 500ms outside of launch spikes; tighten to p99 < 350ms for the launch window with extra headroom.
  * Batch sizes: use conservative batching (max 8 tokens per batch) to reduce tail latency during spikes.
  * KV cache policy: enable prefix caching for your common endpoints; checkpoint interval 2–3 minutes during high churn.

Operational controls we'll add to the addendum: burst-duration cap, daily hours cap, and a soft-eviction grace period with a best-effort checkpoint. If VelaAI needs guaranteed, non-preemptible capacity we should discuss increasing reserved commit.

I'll bring a rough cost delta for transient vs reserved in the call.

—Karthik
Director, Dedicated Capacity — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina@velaai.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 15:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 launch demand — shoulder pool / transient burst ask

Nina — appreciated the projection and the call earlier. Follow-up with a concrete commitment we can offer for the launch window:

Offer (summary) — Launch addendum draft:
- Reserved: 4-unit dedicated slab for steady-state (unchanged).
- Shoulder reserve: priority access to up to 6 transient units from our shared burst pool for up to 4 hours on any given launch day (max 12 hours total across the 3-day launch period).
- Pre-warm: we will run a controlled pre-warm 30 minutes prior to your announced spikes to reduce cold latency.
- Eviction/Grace: 90s graceful drain for prioritized burst instances; if forced eviction required due to superseding critical outages, we provide a failover to a lower-cost model variant to preserve user experience.
- Pricing: transient units billed at 3.2x on-demand rate; hybrid discount applied if you convert transient hours to reserved within 30 days. Detailed numbers in attached PDF.
- Sign: DocuSign link below; countersignature will auto-generate a HubSpot addendum.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/Member/SigningEnvelope.aspx?envelopeId=abc123-docsign
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/VELA-2027-EXP-09

If that all looks reasonable we'll route the addendum to Amit in procurement and schedule the pre-warm windows.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
